data.name: Curcumin
data.description: Turmeric-derived polyphenol widely marketed for anti-aging effects; showed no lifespan effect in ITP testing.
data.description_beginner: The active compound in turmeric, widely sold as an anti-aging supplement. In a rigorous mouse lifespan study, it didn't actually extend lifespan.

studies.title: Evaluation of resveratrol, green tea extract, curcumin, oxaloacetic acid, and medium-chain triglyceride oil on life span of genetically heterogeneous mice
studies.authors: Strong R; Miller RA; Astle CM; Baur JA; de Cabo R; Fernandez E; Guo W; Javors M; Kirkland JL; Nelson JF; Sinclair DA; Teter B; Williams D; Zaveri N; Nadon NL; Harrison DE
studies.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: None of five popular longevity compounds had a statistically significant effect on lifespan. The paper explicitly states the ITP's mission is to publish all results, positive or negative - the exact registry model this Atlas should emulate.
